2607.04907.title: Medi-Gemma: A Hybrid Clinical Decision Support System Integrating Deterministic EMR Analytics and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2607.04907.paper_summary: Deploying Large Language Models (LLMs) in high-stakes clinical settings remains limited by structural hallucinations, weak deterministic reasoning over tabular patient data, and omissions in vector retrieval. This paper presents the architecture and validation of Medi-Gemma, a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for wound pathology triage and workflow automation. The platform introduces a decoupled framework that separates clinical perception from data orchestration while preserving traceable reasoning. Medi-Gemma uses a multi-stage pipeline coordinated by a centralized ClinicalOrchestrator. Data requests are handled without generative inference by a DataManager that cleans unstructured Electronic Medical Record (EMR) files through type coercion. Natural language queries are processed by a hierarchical IntentRouter, which routes requests to deterministic analytics paths executed by a PandasQueryEngine or to patient-specific reasoning managed by a ClinicalRAGEngine using a CPU-optimized vector store. A key contribution is the Ground Truth Injection Module, which intercepts patient-specific queries, extracts numeric identification tokens, queries the structured dataframe via Pandas, retrieves the latest validated clinical state, and embeds this snapshot as an overriding context block in the LLM prompt before generation. Safety compliance is enforced by a deterministic ProtocolManager that maps clinical terminology to fixed evidence-based risk pathways, while a SafetyVerifier phrase filter prevents output rule violations. Validation shows that this architecture eliminates semantic context drift, prevents database compilation crashes, and improves factual adherence to backend clinical repositories. These results support Medi-Gemma as a safer pattern for LLM-based clinical decision support where structured data fidelity, retrieval grounding, and deterministic safeguards are essential.
2607.04907.paper_summary_zh: 在高風險臨床環境中部署大型語言模型（LLMs）仍然受到結構性幻覺、對表格病人數據的弱確定性推理以及向量檢索的遺漏的限制。本文介紹了Medi-Gemma的架構和驗證，這是一個用於傷口病理分診和工作流程自動化的臨床決策支持系統（CDSS）。該平台引入了一個解耦框架，將臨床感知與數據協調分開，同時保留可追溯的推理。Medi-Gemma使用由集中式ClinicalOrchestrator協調的多階段管道。數據請求由一個DataManager處理，該管理器通過類型強制清理非結構化的電子病歷（EMR）文件，而不進行生成推理。自然語言查詢由一個層次化的IntentRouter處理，該路由器將請求路由到由PandasQueryEngine執行的確定性分析路徑，或路由到由ClinicalRAGEngine管理的病人特定推理，該引擎使用經過CPU優化的向量存儲。一個關鍵貢獻是Ground Truth Injection Module，它攔截病人特定的查詢，提取數字識別標記，通過Pandas查詢結構化數據框，檢索最新的驗證臨床狀態，並將此快照嵌入作為生成前LLM提示中的覆蓋上下文塊。安全合規性由一個確定性的ProtocolManager強制執行，該管理器將臨床術語映射到固定的基於證據的風險路徑，而SafetyVerifier短語過濾器則防止輸出規則違規。驗證顯示，這一架構消除了語義上下文漂移，防止了數據庫編譯崩潰，並改善了對後端臨床數據庫的事實遵循。這些結果支持Medi-Gemma作為一種更安全的基於LLM的臨床決策支持模式，其中結構化數據的真實性、檢索基礎和確定性保障至關重要。
